title: Blazing Star
subtitle: Six ships against a cybernetic army
summary: Blazing Star is Yumekobo's Neo Geo shooter, first released in Japanese arcades on 19 January 1998.
body: Blazing Star is Yumekobo's Neo Geo shooter, first released in Japanese arcades on 19 January 1998. Cyborg pilots turn against the artificial systems that created their armies, flying ships with different weapons and handling. The player chooses a craft before entering the side-scrolling stages, giving the journey an immediate personal variation. Large enemies and elaborate bosses fill the route, while the selected ship changes how much of the screen can be threatened and where it is safest to position an attack.

Tapping, rapidly pressing or holding the fire button produces different attacks. A charged shot can be released as a concentrated strike or dispersed across a wider area, and its behavior depends on the craft. The player can therefore change the shape of the attack to suit a formation or boss rather than relying only on movement. Different combinations of speed and firepower give each ship a distinct relationship with the same stage, making another choice of pilot a practical reason to learn the route again.

The game followed Aicom's Pulstar after the studio became Yumekobo. It aimed for a more approachable challenge while developing the pre-rendered visual style and dramatic boss presentation. Harumi Fujita composed the soundtrack. SNK published both the arcade game and its AES home release, which followed in February 1998. Blazing Star carries a recognizable Neo Geo spectacle into the later years of the hardware, using ship variety and flexible attacks to provide different ways through an otherwise fixed sequence of scrolling encounters.
